title: Diazonium chemistry and azo coupling: identifying P, Q, S and T
summary: Walk aniline through acetylation, nitration, hydrolysis and diazotisation, take cumene to salicylic acid by the cumene process and Kolbe-Schmitt, then couple the two and watch the absorption move into the visible.
subject: Chemistry
subtopics: Acetylation as a protecting group for aniline
Nitration of acetanilide and para selectivity
Reduction of diazonium salts by ethanol
Phthalein dye test and the free para position
concepts: A protonated amine is deactivating and meta-directing, which is why aniline is acetylated first
The acetyl group moderates activation enough to stop nitration at one substitution
A diazonium salt couples only with a strongly activated ring
Ethanol reduces a diazonium salt and is itself oxidised to an aliphatic aldehyde
The phthalein test needs a free position para to the phenolic OH
Extended push-pull conjugation moves absorption out of the UV into the visible
formulas: P + H3O+ -> p-nitroaniline; + NaNO2/HCl, 273-278 K -> p-nitrobenzenediazonium chloride (Q)
ArN2+ + C2H5OH -> ArH + CH3CHO + N2 + HCl
cumene + O2 then H3O+ -> phenol + acetone
S + Q / aq. NaOH -> T, an azo dye coupled para to the phenolic O

derivedQuantities.coupling_position: C5 of salicylic acid, para to the phenolic OH

methods: Every intermediate written as SMILES and parsed with RDKit; the counts quoted come from substructure matching, not from reading a drawing
P returns exactly one nitro substructure match, confirming it is a mononitro compound and refuting statement (C)
T returns exactly one aryl-N=N-aryl match plus one nitro match, confirming the azo chromophore

The para position of salicylic acid located programmatically: starting from the phenolic oxygen and walking three ring atoms lands on C5, which carries one hydrogen - the structural requirement for the phthalein test
The phthalein requirement itself verified against independent sources, which state that p-cresol fails the test precisely because its para position is blocked

Reaction of a diazonium salt with ethanol verified against independent sources: it gives the arene plus acetaldehyde plus nitrogen, so the aldehyde formed is aliphatic and statement (A) fails on the word 'aromatic'
Formula bookkeeping across both routes: aniline C6H7N -> acetanilide C8H9NO -> P C8H8N2O3 -> p-nitroaniline C6H6N2O2 -> Q C6H4N3O2+; cumene C9H12 -> phenol C6H6O -> S C7H6O3; T C13H9N3O5

Distractor audit: (A) is half true because an aldehyde really is formed, and (C) is plausible because a nitrating mixture suggests forcing conditions - the acetyl group and the 288 K are what hold it to one substitution
Answer derived independently first, then cross-checked against a published answer key and worked solution for this paper, which agree on (B) and (D) and on coupling at position 5

Headless-browser run of the finished page: 43 assertions covering both routes forwards and backwards, formula and nitro counts at every step, the protecting-group experiment, three bench tests including a negative control on cumene, all four fates of Q, the conjugation sweep, the gate, predictions, theme toggle, clean console and zero horizontal overflow at 390 px and 360 px
